newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Feb 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Feb 3.

text.p: NOTE: These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted, and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

With 148 days to go before the British colony reverts to China, editorials in the Hong Kong media concentrated on the Beijing-controlled Preparatory Committee's decision to scrap a number of Hong Kong's human rights laws and the conclusion of the Sino-U.S. textile trade talks.

-- The English language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST said whether the decision to scrap the ordinances would benefit Hong Kong did not seem to have weighed much on the minds of the Preparatory Committee members who voted.

The future chief executive Tung Chee-hwa must reconcile the contradiction in the community over the two human rights ordinances. The liberal camp wants the thrust of the ordinances to stay to protect individual freedoms. The future Hong Kong governent with Tung at the helm, apparently prefers less liberal laws in order to maintain social order.

So it is hoped that by July 1 Tung, after consultations with different sectors of society, will come up with ordinances that will strike a balance between maintaining social order and preserving civil liberties.

-- The ECONOMIC TIMES said the textile agreement would reduce conflicts in the trade in the next four years. Hong Kong businessmen could sigh a deep sigh of relief for the time being. But the paper believes further conflicts are bound to emerge.

-- The WEN WEI PO said the trade pact was based on mutual trust. Sino-U.S. ties in the next century would hinge on whether the U.S. would talk on a friendly basis or confront China with threats. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6590
